title: Geometric Fixed Parts And Gauss Manin Semisimplicity

items.title: Geometric polarizable Hodge variations on algebraic bases
items.statement: Let $S$ be a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety. A geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation on $S$ consists of a finite-rank rational local system $H$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]), a continuous pure Hodge decomposition of its fibers, or a finite direct sum of pure weights, in the sense of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]], and an algebraic realization on a nonempty Zariski open $U\subseteq S$: there are smooth projective morphisms $f_i:X_i\to U$, degrees $m_i$ and integers $r_i$ such that $H|_U$ is a Hodge direct summand of $$\bigoplus_iR^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i),$$ where $\mathbb Q(r)$ is the Tate structure of [[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]. A Hodge direct summand means the image of a flat rational idempotent that is a Hodge morphism at every point. A morphism of variations is a flat rational map that is a Hodge morphism at every point. A polarization of a pure object is a flat rational bilinear form with the Hodge positivity property on every fiber; it is not postulated for arbitrary local subsystems: a geometric realization carries one by relative ampleness, and Hodge direct summands inherit it. The closures recorded here under finite sums, tensor products, Hodge direct summands and Tate twists, the exterior-power realizability, the duals via the polarization, and the full monodromy-stable integral lattices are proved by the family construction later on this page; that forward mention is explanatory and is not a prerequisite of the definition.
items.strategy: Definitional. Fixes the objects, morphisms, the direct-summand notion and the polarization convention consumed by the fixed-part and semisimplicity theorems of this page. Source route: the continuous-family and algebraic-family definitions and the closure verification of Deligne II 4.2.1-4.2.5 (continuous Q-Hodge families, polarizations, the conditions (4.2.2.1)-(4.2.2.4), the algebraic category of (4.2.4), and (4.2.5)(i)-(iii)). The only claim-like content is the closure/lattice contract, discharged on this page by the family lemma recorded in `justified_by`; nothing about arbitrary analytic variations is imported, and Schmid's unpublished footnote in Deligne II 4.2.6 is explicitly not used. No choice principle is needed: the definition quantifies over finite data.

items.title: Algebraic open inclusions surject on fundamental groups
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $U$ is a nonempty Zariski open subset of a connected smooth complex algebraic variety $S$, then $U$ is path connected and $\pi_1(U,s)\to\pi_1(S,s)$ is surjective for every $s\in U$ ([[def-fundamental-groupoid-of-a-space]]).
items.strategy: Assume AC and derive the countable choice AC-$\omega$ of the two transversality suppliers through [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]. Steps: (1) Stratify the proper algebraic complement $Z=S\setminus U$ by taking, finitely many times, the smooth loci of the reduced irreducible components, using [[cor-generic-smoothness-on-source-characteristic-zero]] and [[thm-smooth-locus-open]], with [[thm-classical-varieties-equivalent-integral-separated-finite-type-schemes]] converting the classical variety to a finite-type scheme; the resulting strata are finitely many disjoint smooth locally closed real submanifolds of real codimension at least two. (2) Replace a based continuous loop, constant on collar neighbourhoods of the base point, by a smooth loop with the same class and perturb it using the tubular perturbation family [[lem-a-tubular-target-produces-a-submersive-finite-dimensional-perturbation-family]] kept constant near the collar; the evaluation is a submersion hence transverse to every stratum. (3) By [[thm-parametric-transversality]] each stratum has a null set of bad parameters in the ball; the finite union is null by [[prop-countable-unions-and-subsets-of-manifold-null-sets-are-null]] and its complement is dense, hence nonempty, by [[prop-a-null-set-has-dense-complement-in-a-positive-dimensional-manifold]] (both on the parameter ball, in the sense of [[def-null-subset-of-a-smooth-manifold]]); choose a parameter outside it. (4) A one-dimensional curve transverse to a stratum of real codimension at least two misses it, so the perturbed loop lies in $U$ and is based homotopic to the original loop in $S$; this gives surjectivity on $\pi_1$. (5) The same perturbation for paths with prescribed endpoints in $U$ shows $U$ is path connected, using that a connected smooth manifold is path connected. Sources: Deligne II 4.1.1 (the topological codimension-two surjectivity of $\pi_1$ for open complements, printed p. 41) with the smooth approximation of loops supplied locally.

items.title: Geometric Gauss-Manin Hodge variations and integral lattices
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For a smooth projective morphism $f:X\to S$ of smooth quasiprojective complex varieties, $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ is a finite-rank local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]), with full monodromy-stable integral lattice obtained from $R^mf_*\mathbb Z$ modulo torsion, and with a continuous pure Hodge decomposition of weight $m$ ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]). A relatively ample line bundle supplies flat Lefschetz operators and a flat rational polarization of this variation. Products, sums, Tate twists, exterior powers and Hodge direct summands have the corresponding geometric realizations and full integral lattices. Pullbacks of algebraic maps between smooth projective fibers preserve rational Hodge structures.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, smooth quasiprojective complex varieties $X,S$ and a smooth
projective morphism $f:X\to S$, with the Hodge types and the polarization
conventions fixed by [[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]] and the
polydisc normal form available from the holomorphic implicit function theorem.

[F1] A projective morphism is proper
([[thm-projective-morphism-proper]]); the closed points of a smooth projective
complex scheme $X$ of pure dimension $n$ form a compact Hausdorff second-countable
smooth complex manifold $X^{\mathrm{an}}$, every standard smooth algebraic chart
becomes a holomorphic chart, every morphism of smooth complex schemes analytifies
to a holomorphic map, and every ample invertible sheaf has a smooth positive
closed real $(1,1)$-form whose de Rham class is the real image of a rational
class ([[lem-smooth-projective-analytification-has-rational-kahler-polarization]]).

[F2] A morphism locally of finite presentation that is smooth at a point admits
there a presentation whose Jacobian has an invertible minor
([[thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism]]), and the holomorphic implicit
function theorem turns such a presentation into local holomorphic product
coordinates ([[thm-holomorphic-implicit-function-theorem]]).

[F3] For a smooth first-order ODE near any base data there are a compact time
interval and a neighbourhood on which the solution exists and is smooth in the
initial state and parameters
([[thm-fundamental-theorem-for-nonautonomous-smooth-odes]],
[[thm-smooth-dependence-of-ode-solutions-on-parameters]]), and the maximal
solution domain of a smooth vector field is open
([[prop-the-maximal-solution-domain-is-open]]).

[F4] A closed smooth manifold has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex, so
its integral cohomology is finitely generated in each degree
([[lem-a-closed-smooth-manifold-has-the-homotopy-type-of-a-finite-cw-complex]]);
on a metric space with a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets, derived
constant-sheaf cohomology is singular cohomology and a nonempty contractible
such space has cohomology $k$ in degree zero and zero otherwise
([[lem-locally-contractible-metric-spaces-have-singular-constant-sheaf-cohomology]]).

[F5] On the proved bounded constructible subcategory, the analytic six operations
include ordinary proper base change, which identifies the cohomology sheaf
$R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ with the fibre cohomology, and the product projection formula
$R\mathrm{pr}_*\mathrm{pr}^*B\simeq B\otimes_kC^*(F;k)$ for a locally trivial
product projection with finite-type smooth fibre
([[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]]).

[F6] For a compact Kähler manifold every de Rham class has a unique smooth
harmonic representative and $H^k(X;\mathbb C)=\bigoplus_{p+q=k}H^{p,q}(X)$ with
$\overline{H^{p,q}}=H^{q,p}$, the decomposition is independent of the Kähler
metric, pullback by holomorphic maps and cup product preserve Hodge type, and
$H^k(X;\mathbb Q)$ carries the resulting functorial rational pure Hodge
structure ([[thm-compact-kahler-hodge-decomposition-via-elliptic-harmonic-forms]]).
The elliptic parametrix and Fredholm theory for a formally self-adjoint elliptic
operator on a compact manifold give the finite-dimensional harmonic space, the
resolvent bounds $H^k\to H^{k+2}$ and the smoothing of its spectral projection
([[thm-sobolev-compactness-and-elliptic-estimates-give-fredholm-hodge-decomposition]]).

[F7] On the primitive part $P^k$ of a compact Kähler $n$-fold the form
$Q_k(a,b)=\epsilon(k)\int_Xa\wedge b\wedge\omega^{n-k}$ is $(-1)^k$-symmetric,
pairs $P^{p,q}$ only with $P^{q,p}$, is positive on $i^{p-q}Q_k(a,\bar a)$, and
is rational when the Kähler class is rational; full cohomology is polarized by
the sign-adjusted orthogonal Lefschetz decomposition, and the construction
applies to smooth projective varieties through their smooth projective
analytifications ([[thm-hodge-riemann-bilinear-relations-for-smooth-projective-varieties]]).

[F9] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ every open cover of a smooth manifold admits a
subordinate smooth partition of unity
([[thm-smooth-partitions-of-unity-exist-on-manifolds]]).

[F8] The cohomological Künneth cross product is an isomorphism
$\bigoplus_{p+q=n}H^p(X;R)\otimes_RH^q(Y;R)\to H^n(X\times Y;R)$ for a PID $R$
when the relevant homology is finite free
([[thm-cohomological-kunneth-isomorphism-under-finite-free-hypotheses]]), and a
local system on $S$ is exactly a functor from the fundamental groupoid of $S$ to
$R$-modules with transport isomorphisms
([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Local product structure. The analytification $f^{\mathrm{an}}$ is a proper holomorphic map, because $f$ is projective by hypothesis and projective morphisms are proper by [F1]; its fibres are closed complex submanifolds, compact by properness. At every point of $X$ the smooth algebraic morphism $f$ admits the presentation of [F2], and the holomorphic implicit function theorem of [F2] exhibits holomorphic charts in which $f^{\mathrm{an}}$ is the linear projection of a product of polydiscs; consequently each fibre is a compact complex manifold. In particular, for every $s\in S$ the fibre $f^{-1}(s)$ is compact and, by [F1] applied fibrewise, carries a Kähler structure. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 Transport and the cohomology local systems. Choose a smooth horizontal complement to $\ker df^{\mathrm{an}}$ on $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ (locally the product charts of step 1.1 provide one; glue the local choices with a smooth partition of unity on the manifold $X^{\mathrm{an}}$ [F9]). For a path $\gamma:[0,1]\to S$ and a point $x\in f^{-1}(\gamma(0))$, the horizontal ODE $\dot x(t)\in H_{x(t)}$ with $f(x(t))=\gamma(t)$ has a unique maximal solution by [F3]; because $f$ is proper, the lifted solution stays in the compact set $f^{-1}(K)$ for a compact neighbourhood $K$ of $\gamma([0,1])$, so by the openness of the maximal solution domain in [F3] it exists on all of $[0,1]$. The resulting transport map $\tau_\gamma:f^{-1}(\gamma(0))\to f^{-1}(\gamma(1))$ is a diffeomorphism, smooth in the initial point by the smooth dependence on initial data in [F3], and an endpoint-fixed smooth homotopy of paths gives a homotopy of terminal diffeomorphisms by the parameter dependence in [F3]. The terminal point maps need not be identical, but their induced maps on cohomology are identical by homotopy invariance. Piecewise smooth representatives and homotopies suffice for the fundamental groupoid: subdividing a path or homotopy into finitely many parameter pieces lying in coordinate charts and using linear interpolation in smaller convex charts gives the usual piecewise smooth representatives without changing the endpoint-fixed homotopy class. Concatenation and reversal give composition and inverses of the cohomology transports. The assignments $x\mapsto H^m(f^{-1}(x);R)$ for $R=\mathbb Z,\mathbb Q$, together with the isomorphisms $\tau_\gamma^*$, therefore define functors on the fundamental groupoid of $S$, that is, $R$-module local systems in the sense of [F8]; this is the local system $R^mf^{\mathrm{an}}_*\underline R$ of the family. [F3, F8, F9, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Identification with the sheaves and integral lattices. On each fibre, and on each product chart of step 1.1, the space is a metric space with a neighbourhood basis of contractible open sets, so [F4] identifies singular cohomology with constant-sheaf cohomology there. The proper base change clause of [F5] identifies the sheaf $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ with the fibrewise cohomology of the local system of step 2.1; the same identification for $\mathbb Z$-coefficients gives the local system $R^mf_*\mathbb Z$. Each fibre is a closed smooth manifold, so its integral cohomology is finitely generated by [F4]; hence the quotient of $H^m(f^{-1}(x);\mathbb Z)$ by its torsion group is a full finitely generated free lattice in $H^m(f^{-1}(x);\mathbb Q)$, and the transport isomorphisms of step 2.1 preserve the torsion subgroups and these lattices. Passing to the quotient by torsion therefore produces the full monodromy-stable integral lattice of the variation. [F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 Continuous pure Hodge decomposition. Fix $s\in S$ and a smooth trivialization $B\times F\cong f^{-1}(B)$ near $s$ obtained by transporting the whole compact fibre along radial paths in a sufficiently small convex base chart using step 2.1, with $F$ the fibre over $s$. The restrictions of a smooth family of Kähler metrics — for instance the pullback along the projective embedding of the positive closed forms supplied in [F1] — give a smooth family $\Delta_t$, $t\in B$, of formally self-adjoint elliptic Laplacians on the fixed compact manifold $F$, with continuously varying uniformly elliptic coefficients on the fixed manifold; here the smooth family of metrics is obtained from the projective embedding into $S\times\mathbb P^N$ by restricting the Fubini-Study form, and the identification of the fibres with $F$ is the product chart. By the elliptic parametrix and Fredholm theory of [F6], the kernel of $\Delta_{t_0}$ is finite dimensional and the resolvent is bounded from $L^2$ to $H^2$; a fixed contour around $0$ separating the zero spectrum gives, for $t$ near $t_0$, convergent Neumann series for $(\Delta_t-\lambda)^{-1}$ and hence a continuously varying finite-rank projection onto the kernel of $\Delta_t$, compare [F6]. Its rank equals $\dim\ker\Delta_{t_0}$ for $t$ near $t_0$ and the kernel dimension is the constant Betti number of the fixed fibre by [F6], so no nonzero eigenspace can occur inside this contour projection; the projection is smoothing and therefore projects exactly onto the harmonic space; applying the same continuously varying projections to the type projections of the forms yields continuously varying subspaces $H^{p,q}_t$ of the harmonic representatives. Since the decomposition is independent of the metric and functorial by [F6], the resulting family of decompositions of $H^m(f^{-1}(t);\mathbb C)$ is a continuous pure Hodge decomposition of weight $m$ of the local system $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ in the sense of the definition. [F1, F6, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Flat Lefschetz operators and polarization. Let $L$ be a relatively ample line bundle on $X$. Its first Chern class lies in $H^2(X;\mathbb Q)$. Apply the positive Chern-metric construction of [F1] to the ample restriction on each compact fibre, extend that metric to a neighbourhood using the smooth trivialization of step 2.1, and shrink the base chart so vertical positivity persists by compactness. Relative to a fixed smooth reference metric on $L$, patch the logarithms of the local metric ratios with a smooth partition of unity pulled back from the base. On a fibre these base weights are constant, so the resulting Chern curvature is their positive convex combination; it is globally closed, represents $c_1(L)$ and restricts on every fibre to a Kähler form with rational class. No positivity in base directions is asserted. Then in the product chart the restrictions to the fibres induce one and the same class on the fixed model $F$ under the identifications $\tau_\gamma$ of step 2.1, because those identifications are induced by the homotopic family of inclusions of the fibres into $X$ and cohomology is homotopy invariant; explicitly, if $\psi_t:F\to f^{-1}(t)$ are the product-chart identifications, then the maps $(t,x)\mapsto\psi_t(x)$ exhibit the composites $i_t\circ\psi_t$ as homotopic to $i_s\circ\psi_s$, so $\psi_t^*(c_1(L)|_{f^{-1}(t)})=\psi_s^*(c_1(L)|_{f^{-1}(s)})$. Cup product and integration are compatible with the transport isomorphisms, so the map $a\mapsto c_1(L)\smile a$ is a flat Lefschetz operator, and the polarized Lefschetz decomposition supplied by [F7] is flat. The forms $Q_k$ of [F7] applied to the primitive pieces give a flat rational bilinear form, since their defining integrals involve only cup products, the flat powers of the Kähler class just described, and the constant sign $\epsilon(k)$; the positivity clause of [F7] holds on every fibre, and the full polarization is the sign-adjusted orthogonal sum along the flat Lefschetz decomposition, hence also flat, rational and positive. This supplies the flat rational polarization required in the definition. [F1, F6, F7, step 2.1, step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 Geometric closures and full lattices. All assertions are made over a fixed open piece of the base, and may be pulled back along a base change to any smooth $S'$ by change of the parameter. Products: for smooth projective $f_i:X_i\to S$, $i=1,2$, the product family $X_1\times_SX_2\to S$ is smooth projective, and the cohomological Künneth isomorphism of [F8] identifies $R^{m}(f_1\times_Sf_2)_*\mathbb Q$ with the direct sum of tensor products $R^pf_{1*}\mathbb Q\otimes R^{q}f_{2*}\mathbb Q$, $p+q=m$, compatible with Hodge type because pullback and wedge of $(p,q)$ forms preserve bidegree by [F6]; this rational comparison uses [F8] over the field $\mathbb Q$, where the finite-dimensional homology groups are free. The ambient product-family cohomology has a full stable integral lattice by step 3.1; intersecting it with each rational tensor summand gives a full monodromy-stable lattice in that summand, since a rational basis can be multiplied by common denominators into the ambient lattice. Thus products and their full lattices are geometric without assuming that the integral cohomology of every smooth projective fibre is torsion-free. Direct sums are realized by disjoint unions of families over $S$. The degree-two cohomology of the constant family $\mathbb P^1\times S\to S$ is $\mathbb Q(-1)$, of type $(1,1)$, and its rational Hodge dual is $\mathbb Q(1)$, of type $(-1,-1)$, by the dual and Tate conventions in the definition. For a realization $H|_U\subseteq\bigoplus_i R^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i)$, twisting by any integer $r$ gives the realization inside $\bigoplus_i R^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i+r)$, which is allowed directly by that definition; the same rational idempotent remains flat and preserves the shifted Hodge types. Thus all integer Tate twists have the stated geometric realizations, without identifying a positive twist with untwisted degree-two cohomology. For a pure variation of weight $w$, its flat rational nondegenerate polarization of step 4.1 gives $H^*\cong H(w)$ as Hodge variations, so the just-proved Tate realization also realizes the dual; the dual of a full stable lattice is again full and stable. Finite sums of pure weights are handled componentwise. Exterior powers are Hodge direct summands of tensor powers cut out by the rational alternating idempotent, which is flat and a Hodge morphism on every fibre; more generally a prescribed flat rational idempotent that is a Hodge morphism on every fibre cuts out a geometric Hodge direct summand of a realized variation. Intersecting such a rational direct summand with the full ambient lattice of step 3.1 gives its full monodromy-stable lattice: a rational basis of the summand can be cleared to integral vectors of the ambient lattice, and flatness of the summand makes the intersection monodromy-stable. Finally, for a morphism $g:X'\to X$ of smooth projective complex varieties, $g^*:H^m(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X';\mathbb Q)$ preserves Hodge types by the pullback functoriality clause of [F6], so rational pullbacks between smooth projective fibres are morphisms of pure Hodge structures. This proves every closure and lattice clause of the statement concerning a single smooth projective family; the Gauss-Manin family itself is geometric and polarizable by steps 2.1-5.1. [F1, F5, F6, F7, F8, step 3.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra]

6.1 Conclusion. Steps 2.1 and 3.1 produce the finite-rank rational and integral local systems with full monodromy-stable lattices, step 3.2 the continuous pure Hodge decomposition, step 4.1 the flat Lefschetz operators and the flat rational polarization, and step 5.1 the remaining closure, lattice and pullback clauses. Hence $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ is a geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation in the sense of the definition, with the stated additional properties. No analytic-variation theorem or Gauss-Manin semisimplicity theorem is imported; the argument is the fibre-bundle, harmonic and Künneth construction of the family categories. [step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 4.1, step 5.1, given, algebra] ∎

items.title: Rational descent of a complex monodromy socle
items.statement: Let $A\subseteq\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb Q}(V)$ be a finite-dimensional rational algebra. The socle ([[def-socle-of-a-module]]) of the $A_{\mathbb C}$-module $V_{\mathbb C}$ is defined over $\mathbb Q$: it is $W\otimes\mathbb C$ for a rational $A$-submodule $W\subseteq V$. If $V\ne0$, then $W\ne0$.
items.strategy:
Route: identify the socle with the zero locus of the rational radical, using regular-trace nondegeneracy. (1) For the finite-dimensional complex algebra $B=A_{\mathbb C}$ with radical $J$, a composition series of the regular module has simple factors killed by $J$ (otherwise $J^rT=T$ contradicts nilpotence, [[thm-jacobson-radical-is-nilpotent-and-the-quotient-is-semisimple]]); with multiplicities $m_i>0$ of the simple types of $B/J$ ([[thm-wedderburn-artin-theorem]], [[thm-simple-modules-over-semisimple-rings]]), the trace of left multiplication is $\operatorname{Tr}_B(L_b)=\sum_im_i\operatorname{tr}( ar b_i)$, so the radical of the regular trace form is exactly $J$, nondegenerate on $B/J$ by matrix units and $m_i
e0$ ([[lem-trace-form-nondegeneracy-characterizes-semisimple-finite-dimensional-algebras]]). (2) In a rational basis of $A$ the regular-trace Gram matrix has rational entries, so its kernel is $J_0\otimes\mathbb C$ for a rational subspace $J_0$, and $W=\{v:J_0v=0\}$ is rational with $W_{\mathbb C}=\{v:Jv=0\}$; this is a module over the semisimple algebra $B/J$ and a sum of simples. (3) Every simple $B$-submodule of $V_{\mathbb C}$ is killed by $J$, so $W_{\mathbb C}$ is exactly the socle ([[thm-finite-length-semisimple-module-characterizations]]); if $V_{\mathbb C}
e0$, a least $r$ with $J^rV_{\mathbb C}=0$ gives the nonzero submodule $J^{r-1}V_{\mathbb C}$ inside the socle, so $W
e0$.

items.title: Characteristic-zero scalar extension of geometric semisimplicity
items.statement: Let $S$ be connected and let $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}$ be a finite-rank rational local system ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]). If $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C$ is semisimple, then $\mathcal V_{\mathbb Q}\otimes k$ is semisimple for every characteristic-zero field $k$ ([[def-semisimple-module]]). In particular this applies to rational Gauss-Manin local systems after complex geometric semisimplicity has been proved. The field $k$ need not embed in $\mathbb C$. Semisimplicity means that every monodromy-invariant subspace has an invariant complement, equivalently that the monodromy module is a finite direct sum of simple modules.
items.strategy: Route: reduce to the finite-dimensional monodromy algebra and test its radical by a rational trace determinant. (1) The rational span $A$ of the monodromy matrices is a finite-dimensional algebra with identity, and $A\otimes E$ embeds into $\operatorname{End}_E(V\otimes E)$ with image the $E$-span of monodromy for every extension field. (2) If $J=J(A\otimes\mathbb C)$ acted nontrivially on a simple constituent of $V\otimes\mathbb C$, nilpotence would give $J^rT=T$, so $J$ kills $V\otimes\mathbb C$ and faithful action gives $J=0$; hence $A\otimes\mathbb C$ is semisimple and its regular trace form is nondegenerate ([[thm-jacobson-radical-is-nilpotent-and-the-quotient-is-semisimple]], [[lem-trace-form-nondegeneracy-characterizes-semisimple-finite-dimensional-algebras]]). (3) The Gram matrix of the regular trace in a rational basis of $A$ has rational entries and nonzero determinant after extension to $\mathbb C$, so its determinant is nonzero in $\mathbb Q$ and remains nonzero in every characteristic-zero field $k$; a nilpotent ideal element $x$ has all products $xb$ in the nilpotent ideal, whence $\operatorname{Tr}(L_{xb})=0$ by [[thm-nilpotent-endomorphism-characterisations]] and nondegeneracy forces $x=0$. Thus $J(A\otimes k)=0$ and $A\otimes k$ is semisimple. (4) A finite generating list of $V\otimes k$ presents it as a finite sum of images of simple summands of the regular module; retaining summands successively decomposes it as a direct sum of simples, which is monodromy semisimplicity ([[thm-finite-length-semisimple-module-characterizations]]). No embedding of $k$ into $\mathbb C$ is used and the argument is choice-free.

items.title: The fixed part of a geometric Hodge variation
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H$ be a geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]]) on a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety $S$. For each base point $s$, the monodromy-invariant space $H_s^{\pi_1(S,s)}$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is a Hodge substructure of $H_s$ ([[def-rational-mixed-hodge-structure]]), and parallel transport identifies these spaces as one constant Hodge structure. Equivalently, the Hodge components of every global flat section are global flat sections. For $H=R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ with $f:X\to S$ smooth projective and an SNC smooth projective compactification $\overline X$ of $X$, the image of $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ is exactly the invariant space.
items.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety $S$, a
geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation $H$ on $S$ in the sense of
[[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]], and points $s,t\in S$ joined by a
path, so that the monodromy representations at the two points are conjugate by
the transport isomorphism
([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]).

[F1] Smooth projective families give finite-rank local systems with full
monodromy-stable integral lattices, continuous pure Hodge decompositions, flat
Lefschetz operators from a relatively ample bundle, a flat rational
polarization, the closure properties under finite sums, tensor products, Tate
twists, exterior powers and Hodge direct summands, and pullbacks of algebraic
maps between smooth projective fibres preserve rational Hodge structures
([[lem-smooth-projective-morphisms-give-polarizable-rational-gauss-manin-variations]]).

[F2] Centered hard-Lefschetz isomorphisms split a bounded t-complex into the
shifted direct sum of its t-cohomology objects
([[lem-hard-lefschetz-splits-a-bounded-t-structure-complex]]); fibrewise hard
Lefschetz for the class of a relatively ample bundle is supplied by the Kähler
identities ([[thm-kahler-identities-give-lefschetz-sl-two-and-hard-lefschetz]]).

[F3] For a smooth quasiprojective $U$ with an SNC smooth projective
compactification $X$, the logarithmic complex gives a functorial rational mixed
Hodge structure on $H^n(U,\mathbb Q)$ whose weights are at least $n$ and whose
minimal weight part is $W_nH^n(U,\mathbb Q)=\operatorname{im}(H^n(X,\mathbb
Q)\to H^n(U,\mathbb Q))$, independent of the compactification
([[thm-logarithmic-complex-constructs-smooth-open-mixed-hodge-structures]]); the
existence of SNC compactifications and of a common dominating model is
[[lem-smooth-quasiprojective-varieties-admit-snc-projective-compactifications]].

[F4] Morphisms of rational mixed Hodge structures are strict for $W$ and $F$,
and a morphism from weights at least $n$ to weights at most $n$ has pure image
of weight $n$ ([[lem-morphisms-of-mixed-hodge-structures-are-strict]]).

[F5] A nonempty Zariski open subset of a connected smooth complex algebraic
variety is path connected and its inclusion induces a surjection on fundamental
groups ([[lem-algebraic-open-inclusion-surjects-on-fundamental-groups]]).

[F6] Proper base change identifies the cohomology sheaf of a smooth projective
family with the fibre cohomology, and the Leray identification
$H^m(X;\mathbb Q)\cong H^m(S,Rf_*\mathbb Q)$ holds in the bounded constructible
calculus of
[[thm-analytic-sheaf-six-operations-have-coherent-base-change-projection-and-trace]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Leray edge map in the family case. Let $f:X\to S$ be smooth projective and put $H=R^mf_*\mathbb Q$. By [F3] choose an SNC smooth projective compactification $\overline X$ of $X$. A relatively ample line bundle exists because $f$ is projective, and by [F2] its class acts on the ordinary bounded t-structure by centered hard-Lefschetz isomorphisms, so [F2] splits $Rf_*\mathbb Q\cong\bigoplus_jR^jf_*\mathbb Q[-j]$ in the constructible derived category. Under the Leray identification $H^m(X;\mathbb Q)\cong H^m(S,Rf_*\mathbb Q)$ supplied by [F6], this decomposition expresses $H^m(X;\mathbb Q)$ as the direct sum of the groups $H^{m-j}(S,R^jf_*\mathbb Q)$; the edge map $H^m(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^0(S,R^mf_*\mathbb Q)$ is the projection onto the $j=m$ summand and is therefore surjective. The stalk of $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ at $s$ is $H^m(X_s;\mathbb Q)$ by proper base change [F6], and evaluation at $s$ from the global flat sections $H^0(S,R^mf_*\mathbb Q)$ is injective because $S$ is connected; its image is exactly the monodromy-invariant subspace $H^m(X_s;\mathbb Q)^{\pi_1(S,s)}$. Consequently the composite $H^m(X;\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s;\mathbb Q)$ has image the invariant subspace. [F2, F6, given, algebra]

2.1 Weights and strictness identify the invariant subspace. The space $H^m(X,\mathbb Q)$ carries the mixed Hodge structure of [F3], whose weights are at least $m$; the target $H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ is pure of weight $m$, because $X_s$ is a smooth projective variety and the restriction $H^m(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ is a morphism of mixed Hodge structures by [F6] and [F1]. Strictness [F4] applied to this morphism, whose target has $W_{m-1}=0$ and $W_m=H$, gives that the image of $H^m(X,\mathbb Q)$ equals the image of its minimal weight part $W_mH^m(X,\mathbb Q)$; by [F3] that minimal weight part is the image of $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X,\mathbb Q)$. Combining with step 1.1, the image of $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ equals the image of $H^m(X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$, which is the monodromy-invariant subspace. Since $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)$ and $H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ are pure of weight $m$ and the restriction is a Hodge morphism by [F1], its image is a Hodge substructure; this proves that the invariant subspace is a Hodge substructure in the family case. [F1, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Base-point independence and flatness of Hodge components in the family case. The restriction $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^m(X_s,\mathbb Q)$ factors through the canonical map $E:H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)\to H^0(S,R^mf_*\mathbb Q)$ followed by evaluation at $s$, and $E$ is independent of $s$. Its kernel $K=\ker E$ is therefore one fixed rational subspace, and evaluation identifies $H^0(S,R^mf_*\mathbb Q)$ with the quotient $H^m(\overline X,\mathbb Q)/K$, carrying the quotient Hodge structure, at every base point simultaneously; this is the asserted one constant Hodge structure on the invariant spaces. Now let $v$ be a global flat section of $H$. Since the invariant space at $s$ is a Hodge substructure by step 2.1, the Hodge components of the value $v_s$ lie again in the invariant space, hence are values of global flat sections $w_1,\dots,w_r$; their sum $\sum_iw_i$ is a global flat section with the same value at $s$ as $v$, so it equals $v$ by connectedness. Since the Hodge decomposition of the invariant fibre is the fixed quotient structure of step 2.1, the section $w_i$ is the Hodge component of $v$ of the corresponding type at every fibre. This proves, in the family case, both that the invariant subspace is a Hodge substructure and that the Hodge components of global flat sections are global flat sections. [F6, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Reduction of a general geometric variation to the realization open. Let $U\subseteq S$ be a nonempty Zariski open on which $H$ has an algebraic realization: $H|_U$ is the image of a flat rational idempotent $p$ that is a Hodge morphism at every point, inside $A=\bigoplus_iR^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i)$ for smooth projective $f_i:X_i\to U$; this is the definition of a geometric variation, and each summand is a finite direct sum of weight pieces. By steps 1.1-3.1 applied to each $f_i$ over $U$ (note $U$ is again connected smooth quasiprojective), the statement holds for every $R^{m_i}(f_i)_*\mathbb Q(r_i)$: its invariant part is a constant Hodge substructure and the Hodge components of its global flat sections are flat. Finite direct sums and Tate twists preserve both assertions, because monodromy acts componentwise and the twist changes only the weight; hence the statement holds for $A|_U$. Because $p$ is flat and a Hodge morphism, it commutes with monodromy and with the Hodge decompositions, so the invariant space of $H|_U$ is the image under $p$ of the invariant space of $A|_U$, and it inherits the constant Hodge structure; the Hodge components of a flat section of $H|_U$ are the images under $p$ of the components of a lift and are therefore flat. This proves the assertions for $H|_U$. [F1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Extension from $U$ to $S$. The inclusion $U\hookrightarrow S$ induces a surjection $\pi_1(U,s)\to\pi_1(S,s)$ by [F5]. Therefore a vector of $H_s$ fixed by $\pi_1(U,s)$ is fixed by $\pi_1(S,s)$, so restriction of flat sections $H^0(S,H)\to H^0(U,H|_U)$ is an isomorphism: it is injective because $S$ is connected, and surjective by the preceding sentence. Given a global flat section $v$ of $H$, its restriction to $U$ has, by step 4.1, Hodge components that are flat sections of $H|_U$; each extends uniquely to a global flat section $w_i$ of $H$, and $v-\sum_iw_i$ is a global flat section vanishing on the dense open $U$, hence vanishes by continuity. For each type $(a,b)$, the corresponding $w_i$ takes its values in the continuous Hodge subbundle of that type on $U$. Membership in this subbundle is a closed condition: in a local trivialization its continuously varying projection has kernel describing the complement, and the difference between $w_i$ and its type projection is continuous. This difference vanishes on the dense open $U$, hence on all of $S$. Thus $w_i$ has the prescribed type everywhere; uniqueness of the fiber decomposition makes these global flat sections exactly the Hodge components of $v$. In particular the invariant space $H_s^{\pi_1(S,s)}$, the values of global flat sections, is stable under all Hodge type projections and is a Hodge substructure with the induced pure decomposition. [F5, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 Independence of the base point for a general variation. Evaluation identifies the rational space $E=H^0(S,H)$ with each invariant fiber $H_s^{\pi_1(S,s)}$. Transport along a path identifies these invariant fibers through this one space $E$, since a global flat section is transported to its own value. Step 5.1 proves that the Hodge components of every global flat section are again global flat sections. On the realization open $U$, steps 3.1 and 4.1 identify these type decompositions with one fixed quotient Hodge structure on $E$, and the closed-membership argument of step 5.1 extends those same types to every point of $S$. Consequently evaluation gives one Hodge structure on $E$ independent of $s$, and transport restricted to the invariant fibers preserves that structure. This assertion concerns the invariant constant subsystem; it does not assume that transport on the full variation preserves the moving Hodge decomposition. Finite sums of pure weights are handled one weight at a time, proving every clause of the statement. [F1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: Semisimplicity of geometric Gauss-Manin local systems
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). If $f:X\to S$ is smooth projective with $S$ a connected smooth quasiprojective complex variety, then every local system $R^mf_*\mathbb Q$ ([[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]) is semisimple over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-semisimple-module]]) and remains semisimple after scalar extension to every characteristic-zero field. More generally the complex local system of every geometric polarizable rational Hodge variation is semisimple. The algebraic realization and geometric integral lattice are essential hypotheses; no claim is made for every polarized analytic variation on a punctured disk.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Induct on the rank of a nonzero pure geometric object H, using the complex socle W_C = socle of the monodromy module ([[def-socle-of-a-module]]). (1) By [[lem-regular-trace-kernel-descends-the-complex-socle]] W_C=W_Q tensor C for a nonzero rational flat subspace; intersecting W_Q with the full integral lattice of H and clearing denominators gives a monodromy-stable integral lattice, so monodromy acts on det W_C by +-1 and its square is a constant subsystem of a geometric tensor object. (2) For a complex simple flat T <= W_C choose a flat complement T' by semisimplicity of W_C; the squared determinant line det(W)^{otimes 2} is fixed, so the Hodge torus carries det T and det T' to flat lines in geometric tensor objects by the fixed-part theorem [[thm-fixed-part-for-geometric-polarizable-variations-on-smooth-algebraic-bases]], and the Plucker description recovers that tT is a flat subspace. (3) Irreducibility is open among flat d-planes: a limit of reducible flat d-planes would produce, via compactness of the complex Grassmannian Gr(d,H_C) ([[def-stiefel-space-grassmannian-and-tautological-bundle]], [[cor-heine-borel-in-the-product-topology]], [[thm-continuous-image-of-a-compact-space-is-compact]]), a flat proper nonzero subplane of the limit, a contradiction; hence tT is simple for t near 1 and lies in the socle, so tW=W for t in a neighbourhood of the identity, and connectedness of the Hodge torus makes W a Hodge substructure. (4) A polarization restricts nondegenerately to W (the Weil operator preserves it and positivity forces a radical vector to vanish), giving a flat Hodge splitting H=W⊕W^⊥ with W semisimple; induction on the smaller rank W^⊥ gives complex semisimplicity, and weight components handle non-pure objects. (5) [[lem-characteristic-zero-scalar-extension-preserves-geometric-local-system-semisimplicity]] then gives semisimplicity over Q and over every characteristic-zero field, and [[lem-smooth-projective-morphisms-give-polarizable-rational-gauss-manin-variations]] supplies the geometric and polarizable Gauss-Manin objects. Sources: Deligne II 4.2.6 and 4.2.7 (read in full: the representation is semisimple, and the tW argument with the connected Hodge group), with the rational descent supplied by the trace-kernel lemma instead of the abbreviated argument there.

items.title: A cyclic geometric weight-zero monodromy system
items.statement: Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). The finite étale morphism $f:\mathbb C^\times\to\mathbb C^\times$, $z\mapsto z^r$, for $r\ge1$, gives a rank-$r$ geometric pure weight-zero local system $R^0f_*\mathbb Q$ ([[def-geometric-polarizable-hodge-variation]], [[def-local-system-of-r-modules-and-its-pullback]]). Its monodromy cyclically permutes the $r$ sheets and its complexification is a direct sum of one-dimensional root-of-unity characters ([[def-roots-of-unity-in-a-field]]).
items.strategy: Verification. (1) The graph of z^r=tW^r is closed in C^× x P^1 and the derivative rz^{r-1} is nonzero on the source, so f is a smooth projective (indeed finite étale) morphism by [[thm-jacobian-criterion-smooth-morphism]]; each fibre is r points, so R^0f_*Q has rank r with the sheet-indicator basis of type (0,0), and the ordinary dot product in that basis is a flat rational positive polarization. (2) A positive generator of pi_1(C^×) multiplies a chosen root by e^{2*pi*i/r}, cyclically permuting the sheets. (3) Over C the vectors v_j=sum_a e^{-2*pi*i*j*a/r} e_a are eigenvectors of the cyclic permutation with the r distinct r-th-root eigenvalues, so the Fourier matrix is invertible and the complexification splits as a direct sum of rank-one characters; the characters are distinct, so the module is semisimple ([[def-semisimple-module]]). (4) The geometric semisimplicity theorem [[thm-smooth-projective-gauss-manin-local-systems-are-semisimple]] gives the same semisimplicity over every characteristic-zero field, including fields not containing all r-th roots.
